answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A contract releases the deposit only after the identity completes a randomly assigned task and remains accountable for disputes; proven fraud burns part of it. Splitting one operator into many identities therefore multiplies locked capital and task costs, while honest participation earns the deposit back. Even as demand rises from nadir to zenith, the river of fake accounts is limited by the attacker’s budget, not by account creation.
